title: SLO cadence handoff lab notes
content:
Purpose:
This is an operational lab note: capture a concrete 60-day cadence to hand off SLO ownership, measurement, and runbooks between platform, serving-runtime, product, and SRE. Not a polished playbook — intentionally tactical: meeting notes, stubs, decision gates, and TODOs to iterate quickly with partners.

High-level goals (why this matters):
- Make SLAs/SLOs actionable across teams: clear ownership for alerting, incident response, and remediation work.
- Reduce friction during launches by standardizing handoff artifacts (SLO definitions, queries, runbooks, canary policies).
- Validate a lightweight operational cadence that scales from small features to large model rollouts.

Scope (what we will deliver in 60 days):
- SLO definition template (service, user journeys, proxy metrics, burn rate thresholds).
- Standard telemetry checklist (required traces/metrics/logs + query examples).
- 4-week pilot with two feature teams: one Hosted API surface change, one inference-serving change.
- Handoff ritual: weekly 30-min sync + biweekly tabletop + final readiness signoff.
- Incident playbook integration: ensure runbook links are embedded in paging rules.

Out-of-scope (for now):
- Company-wide SLA legal language.
- Long-running re-architecture work (will surface as remediation backlog).

Roles & Responsibilities (working assumptions):
- SRE steward (Aisha): coordinates cadence, owns final readiness checklist, tracks adoption metrics.
- Product owner (Priya): defines user journeys and experiments for pilot services.
- Serving-runtime lead (Ben): validates feasibility of SLOs for model-serving constraints (KV cache, batching).
- Observability engineer (Diego): implements dashboards, alerts, and required traces.
- Oncall reps (Sana + rotation): validate runbooks and participate in tabletop.

Deliverables + timeline (weeks relative to kick-off):
- Week 0 (Kickoff): alignment meeting with all stakeholders. Distribute SLO template draft and telemetry checklist.
- Week 1: Observability engineer creates initial dashboards for pilot services. Draft runbooks authored.
- Week 2: Threshold review meeting. SRE steward and product owner agree on burn rate thresholds for canary and steady state.
- Week 3: Canary run for feature A (Hosted API) with controlled traffic. Collect telemetry and measure burn-rate accuracy.
- Week 4: Tabletop incident drill for feature A. Capture gaps. Remediation tasks into backlog.
- Week 5-6: Iterate on dashboards/alerts. Pilot feature B (serving-runtime) canary.
- Week 7: Final readiness signoff meeting. Agree go/no-go and rollout guardrails.
- Week 8: Retro and handoff to maintenance cadence (monthly review).

SLO definition template (example):
- service_name: hosted-text-generation
- user_journey: synchronous text generation for api/v1/generate end-to-end latency (client->model->response)
- objective: 99th percentile tail latency <= 800ms per request
- measurement_window: 30d (rolling)
- evaluation_frequency: 1h aggregation for alerting, 24h for executive reporting
- alerting_thresholds:
  - warning: burn_rate > 2 for 15m
  - critical: burn_rate > 4 for 5m or 99th percentile > 1.2s for 5m
- owner: feature-product + serving-runtime (primary), SRE (secondary)
- rollback_policy: automatic traffic throttle + model-variant fallback if burn_rate-critical

Telemetry checklist (minimum signals):
- end-to-end latency histogram (p50,p90,p95,p99) with per-model and per-region labels
- request success rate (by HTTP status and application error types)
- backend model inference time and GPU utilization per-pod
- KV cache hit ratio and effective token reuse metric
- per-route token cost and per-token latency (for cost-reliability tradeoffs)
- distributed traces for >99th percentile requests

Alerting & Paging:
- Alerts should map to runbook links on the alert description.
- Short-lived noisy signals: route to a metrics channel (no immediate page) with automated aggregation.
- Burn-rate critical alerts page SRE rotation immediately with playbook that includes: rollback steps, model fallback, traffic diversion, and customer comms template.

Canary & Rollout guardrails (practical rules):
- Start at 1% traffic for 30 minutes; observe burn-rate and latency trends for 60m after ramp.
- Success criteria to advance to 10%: no critical alerts, burn rate <= 1.5, p99 within 1.25x baseline.
- If anomaly detected: rollback to previous version and open a bridge with SRE + serving-runtime.

Decision gates (what we actually need to sign off on):
- Gate A (Week 2): SLO definitions accepted by product + SRE + serving-runtime.
- Gate B (Week 3/6): Canary success criteria met for pilot.
- Gate C (Week 7): Final readiness: dashboards, alerts, runbooks, and oncall training complete.

Metrics of success (how we will measure adoption):
- Time-to-readiness: days from SLO draft to Gate C. Target <= 45 days.
- Number of incidents prevented by canary detection (tracked in retro). Target: 1 prevented incident per pilot.
- Oncall confidence: qualitative survey of oncall reps after tabletop (>= 4/5).
- Artifact coverage: % of services with template-compliant SLOs after 60 days. Target: 40%.

Known risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Observability gaps (missing traces or per-model metrics). Mitigation: early telemetry checklist + observability triage sprint in Week 1.
- Risk: Excessive noise from poorly tuned burn-rate alerts. Mitigation: initial alerting channel that suppresses pages and requires SRE tuning before escalation.
- Risk: Model-specific performance variance (quantization/latency). Mitigation: add model-variant labels and gating rules in rollout.

Open questions (to resolve quickly):
- Should cost metrics be included in SLOs or handled separately via Optimize? (Priya to propose recommendation by Week 2)
- What is the canonical source of truth for model-variant mappings? (Ben to confirm; impacts alert routing)
- Who signs the final readiness for enterprise customers with dedicated capacity? (Product + Customer Success?)

Immediate next steps (action items):
- Aisha: finalize SLO template and post to Confluence stub (CONFLUENCE-12345) by EOD Week 0.
- Diego: create dashboards skeleton and add sample queries to the doc.
- Priya: identify two pilot services and owners.
- Ben: add model-variant tags to serving telemetry and validate queryability.
- Sana: schedule tabletop drills and invite oncall reps.

Meeting cadence (temporary):
- Weekly SLO cadence sync: Tue 30m (standing)
- Biweekly tabletop: Wed 60m (pilot-specific)
- Ad-hoc bridge for canary anomalies

Notes (working, raw):
- Draft alert query included in dashboard: sum(rate(burn_rate[5m])) by (service, model_variant)
- Remember to add cost-per-token dashboard to help product tradeoffs during rollout.
- Slack channel: #sre-slo-handoff for quick triage.

Appendix: quick runbook checklist (to paste into alerts)
1) Identify impacted service/model and time window
2) Check canary traffic and recent deploys
3) If burn_rate-critical: invoke rollback policy; divert traffic to baseline variant
4) Notify CS/Customer success if incident could impact committed tiers
5) Runbook owner posts postmortem stub within 48h

This doc is intentionally lightweight and will be iterated after pilot feedback. Add notes inline or link PRs/Jira tickets to the linked_artifacts list above.
